subject: Final-mile evaluation delivery & MAP — timeline and usage constraints
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyline.ai>

Subject: Re: evaluation assets handoff — final mile

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. We want to move the evaluation to the ‘final mile’ stage so our ML team can run the 2-week acceptance pass on our models. To make that possible we need:

- A packaged prompt/test-case bundle (with metadata and provenance)
- Short-term access to a sandboxed instance or ephemeral staging endpoint
- A MAP that lists acceptance criteria, retention/destruction schedule, and usage constraints (no external redistribution, derived-model restrictions)

Attached a CSV with specs on the sample subsets we’ll use (retail-sample-specs.csv). Our procurement contact (procurement@skyline.ai) will follow up with PO details.

Can you confirm what you need from our side to start the transfer and a target timeline?

—Elena
Elena Ortiz
Head of Data Partnerships | Skyline AI
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyline.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: evaluation assets handoff — final mile
Attachments: final-eval-pack-v2.zip (pkg, 42MB), MAP-Signoff.docx (docx)

Hi Elena —

Great — we can run the final-mile handoff next week. Proposed high-level MAP and delivery plan below:

1) Delivery (T+2 business days once PO confirmed): we’ll share final-eval-pack-v2.zip via an ephemeral signed URL and provision a sandbox staging endpoint with token-scoped access.

2) MAP (attached): acceptance criteria (accuracy/regression thresholds, sample pass/fail counts), responsibilities (Skyline test leads + Redwood CS), and sign-off flow.

3) Usage constraints:
   - No public redistribution of raw assets or prompt packs outside Skyline organizational domains.
   - Derived-model outputs are allowed for internal evaluation only; no commercial rehosting or resale.
   - Data retention: SkyLine access window = 14 days from provisioning. After access window ends we will revoke tokens and hold a secure destruction step; any derived artifacts containing raw samples must be deleted within 30 days unless otherwise agreed in writing.

4) Security controls: encrypted at rest & in transit; access keys rotate automatically; audit logs for all file downloads. For PII or restricted subsets we recommend using the private deployment path (see Lauren's note below).

Next steps:
- We can provision once PO_5674.pdf is received and DocuSign for the MAP-Signoff.docx is completed.
- If you want the 14-day window to start later, tell us the desired start date.

I’ve attached the MAP signoff doc for legal/ops. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@skyline.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-30T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: evaluation assets handoff — final mile

Elena / team — quick technical clarifications from infra:

- For the restricted sample subset flagged in retail-sample-specs.csv we recommend provisioning as an isolated sandbox in our VPC-private tenant. That avoids cross-tenant caching and gives you a short-lived private endpoint.
- We support KMS/HSM key wrapping. If Skyline requires customer-managed keys, we can accept an external KMS token and attach it to the sandbox (Doc: https://redwood.app/internal/private-deploy-kms-hsm).
- Audit logs are delivered as a time-bound bundle (S3 link) after access revocation; we can include request-level traces for the acceptance window.

If Skyline prefers a hosted ephemeral endpoint instead, we’ll need explicit written acknowledgment of the usage constraints (no further distribution).

Adding Connor for ops onboarding steps and Kim for legal/terms on retention wording.

—Lauren
Senior PM, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
